transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-07 15:21 UTC; Duration: 42m; Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Rajat (Redwood SE), Jules (Redwood CSM), Lina (Aquarelle HoML), Owen (Aquarelle Infra), Sonia (Aquarelle PM)

Auto-Summary: quick run of recent pilot numbers, agreed to share updated sheets, set SE lab to tune cache.

00:00 Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we can kick off — we have about 40 minutes so we'll run through the numbers then go into tuning items
00:14 Lina: yep thanks, excited to see the updated econ numbers from last week, been chewing on them
00:20 Rajat: quick context — we ran the 4-bit quant pipeline on the staging model, and also enabled prefix caching for the top-20 prompts you shared, and ran a batch sweep across the typical request sizes you sent (avg 320 tokens per call)
00:35 Owen: quick Q — when you say prefix cache is that whole convo cache or just prompt snippet cache? we noticed some terms in the doc that said KV cache vs prefix cache and one place it said KV cash (transcription lol)
00:46 Rajat: yeah ha, sorry — KV cache is key-value cache of past key/values in the attention layer, prefix cache is application-layer prefix matching where identical prompt prefixes hit the cache and short-circuit token generation. we tested both patterns.
01:10 Sonia: can you start with the bottom-line tokens-per-dollar? that's the easiest for execs
01:16 Maya: sure — baseline (no quant, no cache) we measured about 3.8k tokens per $1 for the 176b-ish variant under your traffic profile. with 4-bit quantization we saw ~11.2k tokens per $1 — so roughly 3x improvement. with prefix + KV caching together the effective tokens/dollar moved to ~13.8k — so the cache added about 23% savings on top of quantization in our runs
01:43 Lina: that 13.8k number, is that accounting for LLM completions only or also include embedding/other calls?
01:49 Rajat: only model generation tokens were counted, embeddings were separate in your workload (they're a small fraction). we put the assumptions in the workbook — Maya will share that.
02:05 Owen: what's the tokens/sec/$ metric that you advertised? we wanted to compare throughput for peak bursts
02:11 Rajat: tokens/sec/$ is basically tokens-per-dollar normalized by effective throughput for a given batch profile. with batching tuned we reached 28k tokens/sec per $1 in our benchmark for batched workloads (avg latency 320ms). for single-request low-latency path (no batching), tokens/sec/$ drops to ~4.5k because of lower amortization of kernel overheads
02:38 Sonia: so batching helps tons for cost but kills latency a bit — what's the p95 impact?
02:42 Rajat: correct — at batch size multiplicative we saw p95 tail grow about +60 to +120ms depending on max_batch and queueing. at heavy burst loads with adaptive batching you'll see p95 increase more if you allow long queue times. our suggested policy is small max_batch for latency-sensitive routes (like chat UI) and larger batch for async workers
03:05 Lina: given our SLA of 350ms p95 for interactive flows, sounds like we should avoid big batches there
03:11 Rajat: exactly, and you can keep caching on which still saves tokens without increasing generation time for cache hits
03:19 Owen: any rough numbers on cache hit latency?
03:21 Rajat: prefix cache hits are ~5-12ms added (lookup + short-circuit), KV cache restore for long contexts adds ~20-40ms overhead but saves many tokens; overall net latency for cache hit is lower than full generation for longer outputs
03:39 Sonia: curious — what did the quantization do to quality in your eval set? we have a few edge-case prompts that are sensitive
03:45 Rajat: we ran round-trip evaluations with your prompt set — average ROUGE-like score delta was <1.8% but a handful of hallucination-prone prompts saw bigger deltas. we flagged those examples in the workbook. recommended path: A/B the 4-bit in a small percentage of traffic or use it for non-critical routes
04:10 Lina: ok that aligns with our risk appetite. I also want to dig into the batching sweep results, the workbook had three columns but some of the numbers mismatched what we saw locally
04:20 Maya: yes, a couple of the CSV exports had mismatched traffic shape assumptions — we corrected and will send a refreshed sheet. TL;DR: best econ point at your traffic is 32 max_batch with adaptive timeout set to 25ms
04:35 Owen: does that require dedicated? we plan to run this on Dedicated pools but want to know if hosted can meet same numbers
04:40 Rajat: Dedicated gives more predictable throughput and slightly better tokens/$ due to lower multi-tenant overhead; however the bulk of quant and caching gains are available on hosted. Dedicated helps at large sustained QPS — the delta is about 8-12% cost improvement in our model once you factor in reserved pricing
05:05 Sonia: any compliance blockers for us if we go dedicated vs private? we need SOC2 plus customer-managed keys for some flows
05:12 Maya: Private (VPC/on-prem) supports KMS/HSM integrations and full audit logs; Dedicated is still hosted but with isolated capacity and audit exports — SOC 2 is standard across both, but bring-your-own-KMS is only on Private. we'll attach the security whitepaper in the follow-up
05:30 Lina: perfect. back to numbers — are you confident the 23% cache savings hold at scale or was that an artifact of test set duplication?
05:38 Rajat: good call — some of the savings scale nonlinearly with request duplication. your sample traffic had about 18% prompt duplication across sessions; at lower duplication the cache benefit drops. we modeled a sensitivity table in the workbook showing savings at 5/10/18/35% duplication
05:58 Owen: we also send longer context windows (up to 6k tokens) for a subset; how does that affect tokens/dollar?
06:04 Rajat: longer sequences increase per-call cost linearly, but KV caching helps a lot for repeated contexts because you don't re-compute early layers. in those long-context flows we saw effective tokens/dollar increase by ~1.8x vs no-cache when duplication was >20%
06:25 Sonia: any immediate actions for us to protect latency-sensitive routes while getting cost savings?
06:29 Rajat: yes — route-level policies: 1) latency route: no batching, prefix cache only, shallow quant fallback off; 2) background route: 4-bit quant + large batch + KV cache aggressive; 3) canary: small % traffic on 4-bit for interactive to watch quality
06:50 Lina: could you summarize the recommended rollout order?
06:53 Maya: sure — step 1: turn on prefix cache for all routes (low risk), step 2: enable 4-bit quant on background/async routes, step 3: do 1% canary on interactive, step 4: tune batch settings for throughput routes, step 5: evaluate Dedicated if sustained QPS beyond hosted thresholds
07:17 Owen: are there quick wins we can do on our side to improve tokens/dollar before changing infra?
07:22 Rajat: yes — a) compress prompts (strip stop-words and boilerplate), b) dedupe repeated context at app layer so prefix cache hit-rate improves, c) reduce unnecessary long-context windows for ephemeral tasks
07:38 Lina: ok we'll scope a small client-side change to strip boilerplate and see hit-rate change in 2 weeks
07:45 Sonia: do you have any numbers on how prompt compression affects quality? we worry about truncating important instructions
07:50 Rajat: on our tests, careful compression that preserves instruction tokens reduced cost by ~9% with negligible quality impact for most prompts; we flagged a tiny set of templates where compression hurt, we'll highlight those
08:12 Maya: quick pause — I want to call out the benchmark links: 1) pilot-workbook (short link): https://redw.co/pilot-wb-aq 2) perf-deck: https://redw.co/perfdeck-aq 3) benchmark csv: https://redw.co/bm-aq-csv — we'll attach in follow-up email
08:28 Owen: thanks — can you also include the raw p95/p99 traces for the 4-bit runs? we want to look at tail behavior at 90th/99th percentile
08:34 Rajat: yes we'll attach the traces. initial note — p99 increased more than p95 in some configs due to queueing, recommended to watch p99 in addition to p95 for interactive SLAs
08:51 Lina: on the cost model assumptions, can you include reserved pricing numbers vs pay-as-you-go? we want to know where Dedicated becomes cheaper
08:58 Maya: yes, the workbook will include a sensitivity tab: reserved commit break-even at about 650k tokens/day of sustained throughput in your region given current prices
09:15 Sonia: anything else from Redwood side on monitoring? we want alerts on quality regressions if we flip quantization
09:20 Jules: yep, we have eval hooks — you can upload golden prompt sets and we can run quality checks per rollout and alert on delta thresholds. we'll include a sample alert runbook
09:36 Owen: curious on multi-model fallback — if quant variant starts failing quality we want automatic switch to full-precision model without downtime
09:42 Rajat: supported — routing policies can fallback to a sibling model. we recommend canary with automatic rollback on quality alerts and a traffic split so rollback is seamless
09:57 Lina: ok recap please?
09:59 Maya: recap: share updated benchmark workbook (Maya), SE lab for cache tuning + batch sweep (Rajat), Aquarelle to run internal latency tests against staging endpoint and share p95/p99 traces (Owen). schedule lab for Oct 13, send workbook by Oct 12.
10:18 Sonia: thanks everyone, that's super helpful
10:20 Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up in email. bye.

Notes about transcription quality: occasional mis-hear like "KV cash" and some punctuation errors. There were small crosstalk moments minutes 04:20-04:40.

References shared: pilot-workbook (link above), perf-deck, raw traces to be attached.

End of transcript.
